title: Streamline prefetch event-loop and lease demultiplexor
creator: Ava Patel
description: Background: Our continuous-batching pipeline and KV cache layer have recurring tail-latency spikes correlated with lock contention in the prefetch/lease codepath. Investigation shows hot paths where multiple threads contend on a centralized lease allocator and synchronous prefetch calls cause thread-inversion under high QPS. Goal: Replace the blocking lease allocator + synchronous prefetch pattern with a sharded, event-driven prefetch loop per slot-shard and introduce a lease demultiplexor that grants lightweight tokens to callers instead of blocking on a global lock. Expected benefits: reduced lock hold times, lower p99 latency, improved CPU utilization, and simpler failure semantics for KV warmup. Constraints: minimal change to public RPC contracts, must be reversible via rollout flags, fit within 8-point sprint, and be compatible with dedicated/private deployment (no unsafe syscalls).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Canary rollout at 5% traffic shows reduce in p99 generation latency by >= 15% on affected endpoints; 2) lock-hold histogram shows >80% reduction in samples >5ms across slot-allocator metric; 3) no increase in overall token cost or error rate (errors <= baseline+0.1%); 4) all unit and integration tests pass and new event-loop observable metrics are emitted to Console dashboards.
notes: 2026-02-28 - Initial triage: reproduced lock contention locally using synthetic ingress harness (fixture prefetch_stress_v3). Logged heap/lock profiles and attached flamegraphs to the Confluence doc.
2026-03-03 - Design sync: decided on sharded event-loop (one per slot-shard) vs single global reactor. Chosen: per-shard reactor to reduce cross-shard coordination and allow independent backpressure.

2026-03-05 - Trade-offs discussed: event-loop adds single-threaded scheduling per shard which could starve long-running tasks; mitigations: bounded work queue + preemptible background worker for heavyweight work (file I/O).

2026-03-07 - API compatibility: implemented lease token API that returns a lightweight lease_handle instead of blocking; callers can poll or register callback. Added opt-in header 'X-Runtime-Evented-Prefetch: 1' for gradual rollout.
2026-03-09 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8426 (draft). Key changes: PrefetchReactor, LeaseDemultiplexor, ShardWorkQueues, metrics + dashboard wiring.
2026-03-11 - Benchmarks planned: run baseline vs evented on large-model (seq=1024) and short-chat (seq<128) workloads; measure p50/p95/p99, CPU sys/user, steal, lock hold time, and KV warmup latency.

2026-03-13 - Integration note: ensure fallback path to legacy blocking allocator when runtime flag disabled; also add compatibility layer for Dedicated nodes running older kernels that rely on existing mmap layout.
Canary checklist created in Ops runbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1PrefetchOps
testing: Unit tests: new PrefetchReactor and LeaseDemultiplexor are covered. Integration tests: add 'prefetch-smoke' to ci-integration that runs against local KV emulator. Load tests: use existing perf-harness to run 30-minute sustained run at target QPS with spike injection. Add instrumentation to record lock-hold time, reactor queue depth, and number of lease tokens issued per second. Failure injection: simulate KV backend 503 during warmup and assert callers receive fast fallback to blocking rehydrate path.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag gated. 2) Merge behind flag and run small internal cluster e2e for 48 hours. 3) Canary: enable for 5% of traffic in staging region for 24 hours and run perf comparisons. 4) Expand to 25% for 24 hours. 5) Gradual to 100% if metrics stable; if p99 worsens rollback immediately. 6) After reaching 100% in staging, schedule limited production canary on one region during low-traffic window. Ops alerting: page on p99 regression >10% or error rate delta >0.2%.
migration_steps: - Deploy runtime binary with evented prefetch disabled. - Roll out config change to enable reactor on one control plane in staging. - Monitor newly emitted metrics (reactor_queue_depth, lease_tokens/sec, kv_warmup_latency). - If any regression, flip flag off and collect profiles for post-mortem.
observability_items: Emit metrics: reactor_queue_depth (per-shard), lease_token_latency_ms (histogram), kv_warmup_latency_ms (histogram), legacy_lock_hold_ms (histogram) for comparison. Add Console dashboard: 'Prefetch Evented — Canary' with p50/p95/p99 traces and flamegraph links. Add distributed trace span for 'lease_demux.acquire' and 'prefetch.reactor.loop'.
risks: 1) Single-threaded reactor per-shard could delay long-running admin maintenance tasks; mitigation: preemptible workers and bounded queues. 2) Edge-case race between token revoke and checkout that could lead to double-prefetch; mitigation: idempotent KV fetch and lease token versioning. 3) Unexpected interaction with Dedicated autoscaler: ensure reactor backpressure surfaces to admission controller. 4) In private/on-prem, older kernels may behave differently; include compatibility flag.
